reason: The cited evidence (E1) only states that anti-oxidation coatings are 'still required' for Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, which loosely supports the general need for a coating but provides no specific evidence that an aluminide coating forms a protective alumina scale on HfNbTaTiZr, that it preserves mechanical properties, or that a diffusion-bonded coating is achievable on this alloy. The key mechanistic and performance premises are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Anti-oxidation coatings are required for HfNbTaTiZr-type alloys for high-temperature air applications
An aluminide coating can form a protective alumina scale on refractory high-entropy alloys
A thin coating will not alter the bulk microstructure or mechanical performance of the substrate
The coating process (e.g., pack cementation) can produce an adherent, diffusion-bonded layer on this alloy
